issues.subcategory: violation of statistical independence within dyads
issues.description: The study enrolls 240 participants in 120 pairs. Both members of each pair are assigned to the same experimental condition, watch versions of the same film, conduct a joint discussion (the misinformation manipulation itself), and their responses are therefore correlated by design. The ANOVA plan treats all 240 individuals as independent observations, inflating degrees of freedom and artificially deflating standard errors. This is a fundamental violation of the independence assumption underlying ANOVA, and the problem is especially serious because intra-pair dependency is the very mechanism under study. Correct analysis would require multilevel or mixed-effects modeling with pair as a clustering unit, or treating the dyad (not the individual) as the unit of analysis.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels.

issues.subcategory: power analysis effect sizes derived from incompatible response format
issues.description: The power analysis for detecting the memory conformity replication effect uses Hedges' g values from Ito et al. (2019) and Kękuś et al. (2020), both of which employed two-alternative forced-choice recognition tests. The present study changes to open-ended free-recall questions. Open-ended and forced-choice formats yield fundamentally different accuracy baselines, misinformation rates, and variance structures. The effect sizes imported from the forced-choice studies (g = 1.92 and g = 0.38) cannot be assumed to apply to an open-ended format. This invalidates the power calculation for the replication aim and may render the sample size either grossly underpowered or wastefully overpowered for the actual open-ended effect.
issues.quote: The calculation of the necessary sample size may be based on existing results in which the same procedure as that planned in the proposed study was used on a representative Polish sample. The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges' g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges' g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020)... In existing research using the MORI technique a two-alternative forced-choice questions test was used as the main index of correctness of answers.

issues.subcategory: differential exclusion producing systematic selection bias
issues.description: Participants who correctly guess the study hypotheses are excluded and replaced. The authors explicitly acknowledge that this exclusion will occur more frequently in the three experimental groups (which receive informative interventions about misinformation) than in the control group. This creates systematic selection bias: the experimental groups will disproportionately lose the most insightful or memory-aware participants—precisely those most likely to resist misinformation regardless of intervention. This biases group composition in a direction that would artifactually inflate apparent treatment effects. The replacement-until-target-N procedure also constitutes an informal sequential sampling rule without explicit stopping criteria, raising analytic flexibility concerns.
issues.quote: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size. We realize that this may result in more exclusion in the three experimental groups than in the control group.

issues.subcategory: no inter-rater reliability plan for open-ended response coding
issues.description: The individual memory test uses 20 open-ended questions. Scoring each response into four categories—correct, misinformation-consistent, other, and no answer—requires subjective human judgment, especially for partially correct, ambiguous, or paraphrased responses. The manuscript provides no information about whether coding will be done by a single rater or multiple raters, what specific coding rules will be applied, how ambiguous responses will be resolved, or what inter-rater reliability criterion will be used. Without this, the primary dependent variable is not operationally defined to a standard that permits independent replication or evaluation of measurement reliability.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: multiple dependent variables without multiplicity correction
issues.description: The analysis plan specifies that all four indices derived from the open-ended test (correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, total answers) will each be subjected to a two-factor ANOVA. The plan also separately examines accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions. Running multiple ANOVAs on correlated outcomes inflates the family-wise Type I error rate. No correction procedure (e.g., Bonferroni, false discovery rate, multivariate MANOVA) is mentioned, and no primary outcome is designated to anchor confirmatory inference. This is particularly problematic for the confirmatory replication and intervention efficacy claims.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test's scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test's average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.subcategory: no manipulation check for MORI technique awareness
issues.description: The MORI technique depends entirely on participants remaining unaware that they watched different movie versions. If participants suspect or realize this during the film or discussion (e.g., because their partner's answers differ systematically from their own memories), the core premise of naturalistic co-witness interaction collapses. No manipulation check is described to verify that participants believed the cover story about visual acuity glasses or remained naïve to the dual-movie design. Contamination of the blind is especially likely during discussion, when systematic disagreements across all critical details could prompt suspicion.
issues.quote: Thanks to polarized glasses (which resemble ordinary sunglasses) that are worn by the pair of participants, each of them sees a different movie version while being convinced that they are actually watching the same movie clip... We are interested in people's sensory impressions at different levels of visual acuity.

issues.subcategory: DRM word lists not specified
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition relies on the DRM procedure to demonstrate memory fallibility. The manuscript states that 'four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect,' but the actual word lists are not provided. The critical lures to be disclosed to participants ('doctor, window, sweet, thief') are named in the procedure section, but without the corresponding study lists, the procedure cannot be independently evaluated or replicated. 'Window' and 'sweet' as critical lures are atypical in the DRM literature, raising questions about whether the chosen lists actually produce robust false recall rates.
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect... 'Thank you for completing this memory task. Please take a look at your sheets now. See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief.'

issues.subcategory: intervention content insufficiently specified for replication
issues.description: The content of all three experimental podcasts and the control podcast is described only at the level of general topic areas. For the Extended warning podcast, no script, specific claims, or ordering of content is provided. For the Education about memory podcast, only the Schacter seven sins list is named. For the Demonstration and motivation motivational podcast, only a broad theme is given. The control podcast (soft skills related to social attitudes) is entirely unspecified in terms of content, duration, or structure. Without access to the actual stimuli, independent replication is impossible and it is impossible to verify that the conditions differ along theoretically intended dimensions rather than incidental ones (e.g., tone, length, interest level).
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: overlap and insufficient differentiation between intervention conditions
issues.description: The Extended warning and Education about memory conditions substantially overlap in content: both involve podcasts discussing memory fallibility, both present information about why memory errors occur, and the paper itself acknowledges 'teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation.' In the procedure section, the Extended warning group hears a podcast about 'memory functioning and its imperfections' while the Education about memory group hears a podcast about 'the functioning and sins of memory'—descriptions that are nearly indistinguishable. This overlap undermines construct validity: the three interventions may not be testing meaningfully different mechanisms and any null difference between them would be uninterpretable.
issues.quote: Secondly, we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation... Participants in the 'Extended warning' group will listen to the podcast about 'memory functioning and its imperfections'; those in in the 'Education about memory' group will listen to the podcast about the functioning and sins of memory.

issues.subcategory: no experimenter or coder blinding
issues.description: Experimenters administering sessions will know which condition each participant is assigned to, because they administer different podcasts and procedures to different groups. This opens the possibility of demand characteristics, differential experimenter behavior, and biased scoring of open-ended responses. The paper makes no mention of any blinding procedure for either experimenters running sessions or coders scoring the open-ended test responses. Given that the dependent variable requires human judgment (categorizing responses as correct, misinformation-consistent, or other), unblinded coding introduces a known source of measurement bias.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test of the original material.

issues.subcategory: IMP framework inadequately adapted for social/interpersonal misinformation context
issues.description: The Integrative Framework for Memory and Performance (IMP; Blank, 1998) was explicitly developed for the classic misinformation paradigm, where post-event information is delivered impersonally (e.g., a written description). The paper applies it directly to memory conformity, where misinformation arrives through live social interaction with a co-present partner. The social context introduces additional variables absent from the IMP—specifically, interpersonal trust, desire for agreement, identity-based motives for conformity, and the possibility that participants encode the social relationship itself as a cue to reliability. The paper notes the extension is possible ('similar processes may apply') but does not identify which aspects of IMP require modification or may fail to apply, leaving the theoretical grounding of all three interventions underspecified.
issues.quote: The IMP was developed in the context of the classic misinformation paradigm, in which the post-event information is delivered impersonally. However, similar processes may apply to the memory conformity paradigm.

issues.subcategory: subjective certainty measure collected but absent from analysis plan
issues.description: The procedure specifies that for each of the 20 open-ended memory test questions, participants provide a certainty rating on a 0–100% scale. This measure is described as part of the materials but does not appear anywhere in the analysis plan. It is neither listed as a primary outcome, a secondary outcome, nor an exploratory measure. Collecting a measure and not pre-specifying how it will be used creates an undisclosed researcher degree of freedom: whether to report the certainty data at all can be decided after seeing results.
issues.quote: Moreover, for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).

issues.subcategory: within-subjects correlation of r = 0.07 inadequately justified
issues.description: The within-subjects correlation of r = 0.07 used throughout both power analyses is derived from only two prior studies and is remarkably close to zero. Typically, within-subjects correlations in accuracy measures for the same participants reflect individual differences in general memory ability and should be meaningfully positive. A near-zero correlation implies that knowing a participant's accuracy on non-discussed items provides essentially no information about their accuracy on discussed items—an unusual pattern that could indicate the estimate is unreliable. Furthermore, one of the two source studies (Kękuś et al., 2020) shares authors with the present proposal, raising the possibility that the correlation estimate reflects idiosyncrasies of that specific implementation rather than a stable population parameter.
issues.quote: The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07... A correlation r = 0.07 between repeated measures was assumed based on the research described above (Ito et al., 2019; Kękuś et al., 2020).

issues.subcategory: DRM false recall used as a predictor of MORI social conformity
issues.description: The exploratory analysis plans to use DRM false recall performance as a predictor of MORI memory conformity performance. However, DRM false recall reflects associative semantic memory processes (automatic spreading activation in semantic networks) and is largely an individual-differences measure of susceptibility to implicit associative lures. MORI memory conformity involves deliberate social information exchange and subsequent source misattribution in an interpersonal context. These are theoretically distinct constructs with different causal mechanisms. Using DRM performance as a predictor conflates two fundamentally different types of memory errors, and any correlation found would be difficult to interpret theoretically.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: normative influence dismissal insufficiently justified
issues.description: The paper argues that normative influence (yielding to avoid social rejection) plays little role because participants work individually during the memory test. However, the paper itself immediately acknowledges that 'it is still possible that some pressure exists as the participant knows that their answers will be reviewed by the experimenter.' More fundamentally, participants who participated in a discussion where they agreed with their partner may experience social commitment to the agreed answer even when tested alone. The decision to exclude normative influence from the theoretical framework narrows the hypothesized mechanisms in a way that may not be empirically warranted and constrains the interpretation of null results for any intervention.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the participant knows that their answers will be reviewed by the experimenter).

issues.subcategory: undefined threshold for exclusion of 'unexposed' participants and no missing data protocol
issues.description: The exclusion criterion for participants who 'did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner' is vague. There is no specification of how to handle partial exposure (e.g., a participant who heard the partner's answer to 2 of the 4 discussed critical items). Additionally, with open-ended questions, some participants may leave some items blank or provide unintelligible responses. No imputation strategy, minimum response threshold, or plan for handling item-level missing data is described. These omissions leave important analytical decisions unspecified and open to post-hoc determination.
issues.quote: Participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.

issues.subcategory: age and recruitment restrictions inadequately acknowledged as limiting generalizability
issues.description: Participants are restricted to ages 16–35 and recruited through media and internet advertisements. These restrictions exclude older adults—a population that is both disproportionately represented among witnesses in criminal cases and known to show higher susceptibility to misinformation. Restricting to younger, internet-recruited samples (likely skewed toward higher education, urban environments, and digital literacy) limits the generalizability of findings to applied forensic contexts. The paper justifies the age restriction as a control for pair-matching confounds but does not acknowledge it as a limitation for external validity.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet. The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one.

issues.subcategory: contradictory descriptions of Extended warning podcast across sections
issues.description: Section 2.4.2 describes the Extended warning as 'an approximately 7-minute podcast about the fallibility of human memory... warn[ing] against the discrepancy between the event... and the misinformation... [providing] information about the misinformation effect, source misattribution, and the influence of a lack of confidence.' Section 2.5 describes the same condition as participants listening to 'the podcast about memory functioning and its imperfections.' The second description is nearly identical to the description of the Education about memory condition ('the podcast about the functioning and sins of memory'). This internal inconsistency makes it unclear whether the two podcasts are in fact distinct stimuli or whether the same description was inadvertently used twice.
issues.quote: Participants in the 'Extended warning' group will listen to the podcast about 'memory functioning and its imperfections'; those in in the 'Education about memory' group will listen to the podcast about the functioning and sins of memory.

issues.subcategory: underdefined 'disputed' vs. 'non-disputed' categorization
issues.description: The analysis plan introduces a post-hoc categorization of discussed items into 'disputed' (partners disagreed) and 'non-disputed' (one partner agreed with or did not respond to the other), based on the audio recordings of discussions. No analysis is specified for this categorization—it is introduced and then left hanging. It is also unclear whether 'non-disputed' items (where one partner simply failed to give an answer) will be included in or excluded from the main misinformation analyses. The operationalization conflates two different processes: genuine agreement (true consensus) and yielding (one partner giving up). This creates researcher degrees of freedom in how conformity is quantified.
issues.quote: More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave different answers during the discussion of a given item, their answers will be classified as disputed... if Participant A gave an answer (e.g., Participant A said 'red cap') and Participant B agreed with it or did not give an answer it will be classified as 'non-disputed'.

issues.subcategory: causal claims about mechanism from purely behavioral outcome data
issues.description: The paper predicts that three different interventions will work through distinct mechanisms (destroying the consistency assumption, improving source monitoring, demonstrating vulnerability). However, the analysis plan measures only behavioral accuracy on the memory test. No direct measures of the proposed mediating mechanisms are included—there is no assessment of consistency assumption strength, source monitoring quality, or perceived vulnerability to influence before and after the interventions. Observing that an intervention reduces misinformation-consistent responding is therefore consistent with multiple alternative mechanisms, and the theoretical claims about why each intervention works cannot be tested from the planned data.
issues.quote: Extended warning... should make the participants who are aware of discrepancies discard the consistency assumption and make them rely on their own correct memories... the better the metacognitive abilities of an individual and their knowledge about the deficits of memory, the smaller their susceptibility to misinformation.

issues.subcategory: audio recordings of discussions mentioned without analysis plan
issues.description: The procedure states that the collaborative discussion 'will be audio recorded.' These recordings are later referenced as the basis for the 'disputed' vs. 'non-disputed' categorization of items. However, there is no description of how recordings will be transcribed, who will code them, what the coding scheme entails, or how the coding relates to the statistical analyses. There is no mention of whether the audio data will be analyzed beyond this binary categorization or archived for open science purposes. This is a substantial gap given that the discussion recordings represent direct evidence of the misinformation exchange mechanism.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: vague definition of 'correctly guessing hypotheses' as exclusion criterion
issues.description: The exclusion rule states that participants who 'correctly guess our hypotheses' will be removed from the analysis. However, no operationalization is provided: how complete or specific does the guess need to be? Does guessing that 'memory is being tested' suffice, or must the participant correctly identify the misinformation manipulation specifically? Does guessing one hypothesis suffice, or all? This ambiguity leaves a consequential exclusion criterion—which will be applied differentially across conditions—to experimenter judgment at the time of data collection, representing an undisclosed researcher degree of freedom.
issues.quote: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size.

issues.subcategory: rank-ordering of intervention effectiveness not derivable from cited theory
issues.description: The paper makes a specific ordinal prediction: Demonstration and motivation will be most effective, Extended warning intermediate, and Education about memory least effective. This ordering is presented as following from theory, but the reasoning is essentially: Demonstration and motivation combines two elements (demonstration + motivation), Extended warning is extensive but lacks demonstration, and Education about memory has only theoretical content. This is a post-hoc logical decomposition, not a derivation from the IMP (Blank, 1998) or from Sagarin et al.'s (2002) inoculation framework, which was developed in the domain of advertising resistance, not eyewitness memory. The analogy to inoculation theory is applied without addressing how the differences between persuasion and memory conformity affect the predictions.
issues.quote: Based on the research of Sagarin et al. (2002), we tentatively assume that the most effective technique in reducing the memory conformity effect will be Demonstration and motivation... the Extended warning against misinformation is expected to be slightly less effective than Demonstration and motivation but more effective than Education about memory. We hypothesize so because Education about memory only consists in providing theoretical knowledge but does not demonstrate any effects or motivate participants.
